sentence_stem: I would love to come to your party, so
correct_completion: please tell me the time and place.
full_sentence: I would love to come to your party, so please tell me the time and place.
acceptable_variants: let me know when it starts.

options.text: I did not want to go to the party yesterday.
options.why_wrong: This talks about a past event that does not respond to the invitation in the stem.

options.text: the party was on Friday last year.
options.why_wrong: This gives unrelated past information and does not ask for the details that 'so' is leading to.

options.text: I have a cat at home.
options.why_wrong: This is a true statement about the speaker, but it has no logical link to accepting the invitation.

options.text: please tell me the time and place.

grammar_focus: Result clause with 'so' and an imperative request
explanation: After 'so', we need a clause that shows the result of the first part. Here the speaker wants to come, so the natural result is a request for practical details. Spanish speakers may place the request before the reason, but in English the reason comes first and the result follows after 'so'.
translation: Me encantaría ir a tu fiesta, así que por favor dime la hora y el lugar.
